name: Pinard Yellow
lede: Pinard Yellow is a pale, warm yellow recorded by Ridgway in 1912, and it sits so close to the Crayola crayon called Yellow that the two are nearly indistinguishable on screen.

sections.title: A pale yellow, three ways over
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 color standards place this hue on plate IV, hue 21, tone d; it is reproduced from a scan of an aged plate, so the printed color is approximate [1]. The ISCC-NBS system later filed it in block 86, "moderate yellow", and Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary also records it, on plate 9 J 2 [2][3]. Who or what "Pinard" refers to is undocumented in the books our library draws on [1].

Our library flags a near-duplicate: Yellow, the Crayola crayon color cited on Wikipedia, sits only 0.8 CIEDE2000 units away [2]. The nearest other named colors are [[yellow-tan|Yellow Tan]], 2.5 units off, and [[barium-yellow|Barium Yellow]], [[sandy|Sandy]] and [[straw|Straw]] close behind [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Pinard Yellow appears in 57 of our 23,781 paintings, about 0.24 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 48, more common than half our named colors [4]. It peaks in the 1400s, in 6 of 945 paintings, at 2.5 times the expected rate for that century [4]. Inside a painting it most often plays an accent, in 56 percent of the 48 paintings where it carries real area [4].

The earliest match is dated 1434, in a work by Fra Angelico — 478 years before Ridgway's 1912 record of the name, as photographed, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [4]. The gap is a look-alike hue surviving in an aged photograph, not proof that this exact paint existed that early [4].
